base: exact v13 coherent Windows WSA8845 analog-tail boot bundle
question: Does matching Windows qcaucd's bounded post-CLOCK_STOP_NOW frame-generator completion wait preserve the improved v13 cold state across a subsequent PA wake?

windows_evidence.post_stop_behavior: qcaucd polls SWRM_COMP_STATUS 0x14 bit0 at approximately 1 ms cadence for approximately 30 ms before gating the lower SoundWire resource/clock path

linux_delta.behavior: after sdw_bus_clk_stop(), poll SWRM_COMP_STATUS bit0 up to 30 times with usleep_range(1000,1100), then gate hclk; all other v13 behavior and 3000 ms autosuspend timing unchanged

structural_gate.kernel_message: SP11 SoundWire: frame generator stopped before hclk gate
structural_gate.physical_pcm: RUNNING during zero stream and closed after idle
structural_gate.runtime_pm: SoundWire master and both WSA8845 slaves suspended
structural_gate.faults: no SoundWire, state, PA or XRUN faults

acoustic_gate.context: mic-measured PA cycle occurred after one prior complete v16 structural PA cycle on the same boot
acoustic_gate.stimulus: 10 s, 48 kHz stereo S16_LE all-zero PCM, endpoint 1 percent muted

conclusion: Waiting for the physical SoundWire frame generator to stop before hclk gating is a real contributor and materially reduces the catastrophic second-cycle noise versus v13 cycle2/v15, but it remains about 115x Windows and 3.11x v5. The post-stop wait is necessary-direction evidence, not sufficient parity.
